caliber: monotone calibration of a digital measure to a multi-item PRO

Source: R/caliber-package.R
caliber-package.Rd

One latent trait \(\eta \sim N(0, 1)\) drives an ordinal multi-item PRO (logistic graded response model, items scored 0 to 3) and a continuous digital or performance measure \(y\): $$\mathrm{logit}\, P(C_j \ge k \mid \eta) = a_j \eta + d_{jk}, \qquad y = \mu(\eta) + e, \quad e \sim N(0, \sigma(\eta)^2), \quad \log \sigma(\eta) = g_0 + g_1 \eta,$$ with \(\mu(\eta) = \sum_m \beta_m B_m(\eta)\) a non-increasing cubic B-spline (24 coefficients, 20 interior knots on \([-4, 4]\)). Higher \(\eta\) means more of the PRO construct (worse sleep, more mobility difficulty); the digital measure falls as \(\eta\) rises.

Details

The curve is fitted by monotonic likelihood boosting of B-splines (Leitenstorfer and Tutz 2007) with the AIC stop, in one of three ways that differ only in how \(\eta\) is handled (see [fit_ms()]):

MS-Joint

concurrent calibration: GRM items and curve estimated together, \(\eta\) integrated out over \(p(\eta \mid C, y)\);

MS-EAP

EAP plug-in: GRM on the PRO alone, EAP scores treated as known;

MS-Fixed

fixed-item calibration: GRM on the PRO alone, items then fixed, \(\eta\) integrated out (the recommended primary analysis).

Throughout the code the digital measure is called `sqi` (the sleep-quality index of the worked example); any continuous measure that falls with the latent trait can be used (gait speed in the NHANES example).
